title: In characteristic p a geometrically reduced field extension is separable
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ and let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] such that for every field extension $L/k$ the ring $K\otimes_kL$ (the tensor product of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], with multiplication $(a\otimes\mu)(a'\otimes\mu')=aa'\otimes\mu\mu'$ and unit $1\otimes1$) is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent elements). Then $K$ is separable over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (2): every subextension $k\subset K'\subset K$ with $K'$ finitely generated as a field over $k$ is separably generated over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, line 10360), implication (4) => (1), proved in the source as (4) => (3) => (2) => (1) with Lemma Tag 0H71 (lemma-mini-separability, line 10296) for (2) => (1); 'geometrically reduced' (4) is Definition Tag 030S (definition-geometrically-reduced), written out here

proof.text: (The field $k^{1/p}$.) Let $\iota:k\to\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] (every field has one). As $p\cdot1=0$ in $\Omega$, the Frobenius $F_\Omega:u\mapsto u^p$ is a ring homomorphism [def-weil-ring-frobenius], injective since $\Omega$ is a field. Put $L=\{\mu\in\Omega:\mu^p\in\iota(k)\}$. It contains $\iota(k)$ ($\iota(c)^p=\iota(c^p)$) and is closed under sums, differences and products (as $F_\Omega$ is a ring homomorphism) and under inverses of nonzero elements ($(\mu^{-1})^p=(\mu^p)^{-1}$), so $L$ is a subfield of $\Omega$ and, with $\iota$, a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]; this is $k^{1/p}$. For $c\in k$ the polynomial $T^p-\iota(c)$ has a root $\mu\in\Omega$ ($\Omega$ is algebraically closed; for $c=0$ take $\mu=0$), and $\mu\in L$; it is unique by injectivity of $F_\Omega$. Write $c^{1/p}\in L$ for it, so $(c^{1/p})^p=c$ (identifying $k$ with $\iota(k)$), and $c^{1/p}=0$ only if $c=(c^{1/p})^p=0$.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph before Lemma Tag 030W (lines 10352-10357): '$k^{1/p}$ ... is the subfield of an algebraic closure of $k$ generated by the $p$th roots of elements of $k$'; the closure of $L$ under the field operations is written out by the agent

proof.text: ((4) $\Rightarrow$ (3).) By hypothesis, applied to the field extension $L=k^{1/p}$ of step 1, the ring $A=K\otimes_kL$ [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] is reduced. $A$ is a commutative ring with $(a\otimes\mu)(a'\otimes\mu')=aa'\otimes\mu\mu'$ and unit $1\otimes1$; it is an $L$-vector space by $\lambda\cdot(a\otimes\mu)=a\otimes\lambda\mu$ [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]; and for $c\in k$ one has $ca\otimes\mu=a\otimes c\mu$ (the tensor product is over $k$). In particular $p\cdot1_A=(p\cdot1_k)(1\otimes1)=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W (line 10360): 'The implication (4) => (3) is immediate' (line 10376)

proof.text: (The identity $x^p=m(x)\otimes1$.) Let $b_1,\dots,b_m\in K$ and $c_1,\dots,c_m\in k$, and put $x=\sum_{i=1}^mb_i\otimes c_i^{1/p}\in A$ (step 1). Since $A$ is commutative with $p\cdot1_A=0$ (step 2), its Frobenius $F_A:y\mapsto y^p$ is a ring homomorphism [def-weil-ring-frobenius], so $x^p=\sum_i(b_i\otimes c_i^{1/p})^p=\sum_ib_i^p\otimes(c_i^{1/p})^p=\sum_ib_i^p\otimes c_i=\big(\sum_ic_ib_i^p\big)\otimes1$, the last equality because $c_i\in k$ passes across the tensor sign over $k$ (step 2). (This is the source's $x^p=m(x)\otimes1$ for the map $m:\lambda\otimes\mu\mapsto\lambda^p\mu^p$, evaluated on $x$; only this value of $m$ is used below, so $m$ need not be constructed on all of $A$.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W, paragraph 'Assume (3)' (line 10379): 'Consider the ring homomorphism $m:K\otimes_kk^{1/p}\to K$ given by $\lambda\otimes\mu\mapsto\lambda^p\mu^p$. Note that $x^p=m(x)\otimes1$'

proof.text: ((3) $\Rightarrow$ (2).) Let $b_1,\dots,b_m\in K$ be pairwise distinct and linearly independent over $k$, and let $c_1,\dots,c_m\in k$ with $\sum_ic_ib_i^p=0$; we show all $c_i=0$. For $x=\sum_ib_i\otimes c_i^{1/p}$, step 3 gives $x^p=0\otimes1=0$, so $x$ is nilpotent and, $A$ being reduced (step 2), $x=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] the linearly independent set $\{b_1,\dots,b_m\}$ is contained in a $k$-basis $\mathcal B$ of $K$, and by [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] the family $(b\otimes1)_{b\in\mathcal B}$ is an $L$-basis of $A=K\otimes_kL$; in particular $b_1\otimes1,\dots,b_m\otimes1$ are linearly independent over $L$. Now $0=x=\sum_ic_i^{1/p}\cdot(b_i\otimes1)$ for the $L$-vector space structure of step 2, so every $c_i^{1/p}=0$, hence $c_i=0$ by step 1. Thus $K$ satisfies condition (2) of Stacks 030W: for all pairwise distinct $b_1,\dots,b_m\in K$ linearly independent over $k$, the elements $b_1^p,\dots,b_m^p$ are linearly independent over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030W, paragraph 'Assume (3)' (lines 10379-10391): 'Since $K\otimes_kk^{1/p}$ is reduced we see $m$ is injective. If $\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}\subset K$ is $k$-linearly independent, then $\{a_1\otimes1,\dots,a_m\otimes1\}$ is $k^{1/p}$-linearly independent. By injectivity of $m$ we deduce that no nontrivial $k$-linear combination of $a_1^p,\dots,a_m^p$ is zero'

proof.text: ((2) $\Rightarrow$ (1).) Let $k\subset K'\subset K$ be a subextension with $K'=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ finitely generated over $k$; $K'$ is a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] of characteristic $p$. If $b_1,\dots,b_m\in K'$ are pairwise distinct and linearly independent over $k$, they are so as elements of $K$ (a relation $\sum c_ib_i=0$ with $c_i\in k$ is the same in $K'$ and in $K$), so by step 4 there is no nontrivial relation $\sum_ic_ib_i^p=0$ with $c_i\in k$, in $K$ and hence in $K'$. Thus $K'/k$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-p-power-independence-separably-generated], which shows that $K'$ is separably generated over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1). As $K'$ was an arbitrary finitely generated subextension, $K$ is separable over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (2).
